title: StoreMessage
description: Messages of the store contract: where the lake is, statements and reads with bound parameters, snapshots, commit results, maintenance reports and errors. Read results are Arrow record-batch streams (see README).

Parameter.description: A named parameter bound to `$name` in the SQL. The value is text converted to the declared DuckDB type; exact values are never JSON numbers.

StatementRequest.description: One SQL statement executed in a write transaction.

timeout_ms.description: Time limit in milliseconds, waiting for a slot included (default: the lake's default_timeout_ms).

ReadRequest.description: One SELECT statement read once, as of a snapshot, as an Arrow record-batch stream.

timeout_ms.description: Time limit in milliseconds, waiting for a slot included (default: the lake's default_timeout_ms).

CommitResult.description: The snapshot a committed transaction created, or null when it changed nothing.

MaintenanceReport.description: What one maintenance call did: snapshots older than its cutoff expired, small files merged, files with many deletes rewritten, files no snapshot uses deleted, and orphaned files deleted. `oldest_snapshot` is the oldest snapshot kept; reads pinned to an older one fail with `STORE_SNAPSHOT_EXPIRED`.

LocalLakeLocation.description: A DuckLake lake with a DuckDB-file catalog (one process): the catalog at <catalog_path>, by default <path>/catalog.ducklake, and data files under <data_path>, by default <path>/data/.

catalog_path.description: Absolute path of the catalog file, when it is not <path>/catalog.ducklake. The file sandbox gains exactly that file and its write-ahead log.

data_path.description: Where data files are written, when not <path>/data/: an absolute local folder, or object storage with storage: s3://bucket/prefix/, gs://bucket/prefix/ or az://container/prefix/.

encrypted.description: DuckLake data-file encryption (ENCRYPTED), used when the lake is created.

SqliteLakeLocation.description: A DuckLake lake with a SQLite-file catalog (several processes on one machine): the catalog at <path>, data files under <data_path>. The file sandbox gains exactly the catalog file and its -wal, -shm and -journal files.

encrypted.description: DuckLake data-file encryption (ENCRYPTED), used when the lake is created.

PostgresLakeLocation.description: A DuckLake lake whose catalog lives in PostgreSQL, so several processes can read and write it. The password is never part of the location: it is read from the environment variable named by password_env. A host other than the local machine (localhost, 127.0.0.1, ::1, a Unix-socket directory) needs sslmode=verify-full (STORE_TLS_REQUIRED otherwise).

connection.description: libpq key=value connection string without a password, e.g. host=db port=5432 dbname=lake user=analytics sslmode=verify-full

metadata_schema.description: PostgreSQL schema holding the catalog tables (default: public)

encrypted.description: DuckLake data-file encryption (ENCRYPTED), used when the lake is created.

type.description: DuckDB type name, e.g. DECIMAL(18,4) or TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE

ResultJson.description: A read result encoded as JSON without losing exactness (README: encoding rules). Rows are positional arrays matching columns.

FileSourceAttachment.description: A file source (Parquet, CSV, DuckDB) the lake reads inside write transactions, by name: `<name>.data` for parquet and csv (every matching file as one table, columns united by name), `<name>.<schema>.<table>` (or `<name>.<table>` for `main`) for a DuckDB file attached read-only. Reads never see sources. Only the declared paths become readable.

name.description: The connection name; becomes a catalog name in SQL.

path.description: Absolute path; parquet and csv may use a glob (`*`, `?`, `[...]`, `**`) in their file name or folders.

SqliteSourceAttachment.description: A SQLite database file attached read-only: `<name>.<table>`. Columns declared DECIMAL or NUMERIC (stored by SQLite as floating point) are refused when a write reads them (`UNSUPPORTED_SOURCE_TYPE`).

name.description: The connection name; becomes a catalog name in SQL.

path.description: Absolute path; parquet and csv may use a glob (`*`, `?`, `[...]`, `**`) in their file name or folders.

PostgresSourceAttachment.description: A PostgreSQL database attached read-only (also `default_transaction_read_only` on its session): `<name>.<table>` when `schema` is given, otherwise `<name>.<schema>.<table>`. The password is read from the environment variable `password_env` and never appears in errors. Columns `numeric` without precision and `money` are refused when a write reads them (`UNSUPPORTED_SOURCE_TYPE`). A host other than the local machine (localhost, 127.0.0.1, ::1) needs sslmode verify-full (STORE_TLS_REQUIRED otherwise).

name.description: The connection name; becomes a catalog name in SQL.

sslmode.description: libpq sslmode: verify-full, or disable for the local machine only; absent, libpq's default (local machine only).

sslrootcert.description: With verify-full: `system` (the default) or `${env:NAME}`, a variable holding the path of a CA file, read by the store when the lake opens.

SourceAttachment.description: A source the lake reads inside write transactions, by name; reads never see sources.

S3Storage.description: Object storage for data files, reached through DuckDB's official httpfs extension with a temporary secret scoped to data_path. The credentials are read from the environment variables named here. use_ssl false is refused unless the endpoint is the local machine (STORE_TLS_REQUIRED).

GcsStorage.description: Google Cloud Storage for data files (gs://bucket/prefix/), reached through DuckDB's official httpfs extension with HMAC keys (Cloud Storage interoperability) as a temporary secret scoped to data_path. The keys are read from the environment variables named here. use_ssl false is refused unless the endpoint is the local machine (STORE_TLS_REQUIRED).

AzureStorage.description: Azure Blob Storage for data files (az://container/prefix/), reached through DuckDB's official azure extension with a connection string as a temporary secret scoped to data_path. The connection string is read from the environment variable named here; its protocol must be https (DefaultEndpointsProtocol, and a BlobEndpoint if it has one) unless the endpoint is the local machine (STORE_TLS_REQUIRED). A connection string that is not key=value pairs or names no AccountName is refused (STORE_STATEMENT_INVALID), without showing it.

ObjectStorage.description: Object storage for the lake's data files: S3-compatible, Google Cloud Storage or Azure Blob Storage.

StatisticsRequest.description: The file statistics of lake tables as of one snapshot, read from the lake's own catalog on the store's connection: never a path or any other catalog detail. For estimating read cost as an upper bound only (semantic-engine.md §8).

TableName.description: A lake table: `table` (schema `main`) or `schema.table`, as written in the lake.

ColumnStatistics.description: One column of one data file. `min` and `max` are present only when the lake records them as exact, as text in the column's own DuckDB type; `nulls` when the lake records it.

FileStatistics.description: One data file the snapshot reads: its row count before deletes (an upper bound of its live rows) and its size.

TableStatistics.description: One table as of the snapshot: its data files, and the rows kept in the catalog itself (data inlining), which have no column statistics. `complete` is false when a file the snapshot reads has no row count: then no upper bound exists.

StatisticsResult.description: The answer to one `StatisticsRequest`, one entry per table asked, in order.

TablesRequest.description: Every lake table alive at one snapshot, with its columns as of that snapshot, read from the lake's own catalog on the store's connection (#358): the schema a semantic model compiles against. Never a path, a file or any other catalog detail.

TableColumn.description: One column as of the snapshot: its name, its DuckDB type, and whether the lake allows NULL in it.

LakeTable.description: One lake table as of the snapshot, its columns in order.

TablesResult.description: The answer to one `TablesRequest`: every table alive at the snapshot, ordered by schema and table.

ChangesRequest.description: What changed in lake tables between two snapshots (#355): whether each table changed at all (rows or columns) after `since` up to `snapshot`, from the lake's own change history, and how many of the rows it had at `since` it no longer has, compared by value by DuckDB reading the table at both versions. Counts only, never a value. With `count_removed: false`, only the catalog is read (#364).

count_removed.description: False: only `changed`, from the catalog alone, and no row of any table is read (`removed_rows` is absent). Default true.

TableChanges.description: One table between `since` and `snapshot`. `changed`: any row or column changed, or the table was created, dropped or replaced. `removed_rows`: rows present at `since` and missing at `snapshot`, by value as a multiset (a dropped table lost every row; one created since had none); absent when a column it had at `since` is gone.

ChangesResult.description: The answer to one `ChangesRequest`, one entry per table asked, in order.

ExistingLakeAttachment.description: An existing DuckLake that another system owns and writes, attached read-only in a DuckDB instance of its own (ADR-0027 §3, P2-30). The catalog and sandbox checks are made before any of its data is read; see README, "Existing DuckLake".

location.description: The lake's catalog and data location. `encrypted` is the owner's setting and is refused here.

roles_in_use.description: Every PostgreSQL role name used by another connection of the instance (catalogs and sources) and by every managed lake's catalog. A PostgreSQL catalog whose role is listed is refused.

protected_files.description: Absolute paths of the files no SQLite catalog may be a hard link to (the protected set). Each one's -wal, -shm, -journal and .wal files are protected with it.

protected_locations.description: Every location of the protected set across the instance (P2-30 PR 2): the instance folders; each registered project's folder, managed lake data location and catalog file, file sources' paths (a glob by its folder), and the locations and catalog files of its existing lakes other than this lake. An absolute local path, or an s3://, gs:// or az:// prefix. The lake's data location and SQLite catalog must neither equal, contain nor lie inside one, and a local one must be on a file system that holds none of them. Optional in the schema (new in P2-30 PR 2, compatible), required by the store: an attachment without it is refused, since the lake cannot be shown apart from the protected set.
